home.name: Georgios Feidakis
home.title: A Senior Software Engineer.
home.intro: I am a software engineer with a passion for web development. I have always been drawn to the front-end side of things, even though I have some understanding in the back-end side of things too. For the past several years, I have focused my learning and practice on Angular, a powerful JavaScript framework for building dynamic, responsive, and scalable web applications.

about.heading: About me
paragraphs: I am a software engineer who is passionate about creating elegant, efficient, and user-friendly web applications. With over 5 years of experience in the industry, I have developed a strong foundation in various programming languages, frameworks, and tools, including HTML / CSS, JS / TS, Angular etc.

I've always loved computers and tinkering with them, which led me to discover my passion for programming and coding. Despite studying Electrical and Electronic Engineering, I never lost sight of this passion and decided to pursue a career in software engineering to combine my academic background with my creative and technical interests.

When I'm not coding, you'll likely find me out on a run or hitting the gym. I believe that regular exercise is not only essential for physical health, but also for mental clarity, stress relief, and overall well-being.

projects.name: Portfolio & CV ecosystem
projects.description: This site and my online CV, built as one system: a single content source feeds both, so a text or theme change publishes everywhere without touching either app.
highlights: Standalone components and signals; content and design tokens fetched at runtime from the CV repo.
Zero content in the app repo, so copy changes never require a frontend deploy.
Deployed by GitHub Actions on every push.

caseStudy.headline: Portfolio and online CV built as one system, so a wording or theme change publishes to both without a frontend deploy.
caseStudy.context: I keep a public portfolio and an online CV. Maintained separately, the two drift: a job changes, one gets updated, the other quietly goes stale. I rebuilt them in 2026 as one system with a single content source.
caseStudy.goal: One place to change text or visual style, with the change appearing on both surfaces.
caseStudy.role: Sole author: the content model, the Angular application, the shared design tokens and the deployment.
approach: Standalone components and signals; content and design tokens fetched at runtime from the CV repo.
Zero content in the app repo, so copy changes never require a frontend deploy.
Deployed by GitHub Actions on every push.
results: A wording change is an edit to one content file; the portfolio picks it up on the next page load, with no frontend release.
Design tokens are published alongside the content, so both sites share one palette by construction.
Every push deploys through GitHub Actions; there is no manual release step.

projects.name: CV generator with automated A4 PDF
projects.description: A static-site generator that turns one content file into an online CV, a true-A4 print page and a downloadable PDF, so the published PDF can never drift from the site.
highlights: Content lives in plain key/value files and is validated against per-field length limits, failing the build when copy would break the layout.
Print stylesheet renders real 210mm A4 rather than relying on the browser's shrink-to-fit.
The PDF is generated by headless Chrome during the build and published with the site.

caseStudy.headline: One content source builds the online CV, a true-A4 print page and the downloadable PDF, so the PDF cannot go stale.
caseStudy.context: Keeping an online CV and a PDF in sync by hand fails quietly: the page gets edited, the PDF does not, and the version people receive stops matching the one on the web.
caseStudy.goal: Generate every output from one content source, and make the printed page a real A4 document rather than a browser page squeezed onto paper.
caseStudy.role: Sole author: the content model and its validation, the SCSS and print stylesheet, the Node build, the tests and the CI pipeline.
approach: Content lives in plain key/value files and is validated against per-field length limits, failing the build when copy would break the layout.
Print stylesheet renders real 210mm A4 rather than relying on the browser's shrink-to-fit.
The PDF is generated by headless Chrome during the build and published with the site.
results: The site, the print page and the PDF are generated from the same content, so the download always matches what is published.
Copy that would overflow the layout fails the build instead of shipping, thanks to per-field length limits.
The print stylesheet targets real 210mm A4, so the PDF is a proper document rather than a scaled-down screen layout.

blogs.title: My Fitness Transformation Story
blogs.description: I used to believe that losing weight wasn't possible for me, but in 2017, I decided to challenge that belief and started running every day. After losing 25 kilograms in a year, I joined a gym and began lifting weights. It wasn't easy, but I never gave up. Even during the COVID lockdowns, I found ways to stay active and stay on track. Now, my fitness journey is a part of my lifestyle, and I'm proud of the person I've become.
